why: The LIVE half of the declared-vs-live control (issue #1415). `disabled: true` in a *-trigger.yaml is a DECLARATION; until this file existed nothing in `make verify` read what the project actually runs, so `check-cloudbuild.sh` was green while every control-plane trigger was ENABLED. This is a RECORDED measurement, not a live call: the gate compares the declarations against it offline and deterministically, and never claims to have contacted GCP. Refresh it with the command below and commit the result -- a refusal in the gate names this file and that command.
scope: every trigger whose repository is kushin77/agent-orchestrator (repositoryEventConfig.repository ends /repositories/agent-orchestrator), projected to the fields this control needs; raw capture sha256 a5d5263e56d2a3d13ea61e064f35efdad7ada41247bafaed61bd0f7598b607a4
disabled_field: Cloud Build omits `disabled` entirely when the trigger is ENABLED (measured against this same capture: disabled=true IS present on two unrelated triggers). `false` below is that absence, normalised -- it is not a field the API returned as false.

triggers.name: control-plane-web-image
triggers.promoted_flag: none -- this declaration carries no _ENABLE_* key; the trigger state is the only switch
